newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Sept 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Sept 5.

text.p: - Palace officials and Congress leaders will prepare an action plan based on "possible implications of the recent incidents in Iraq on the supply and prices of oil", executive secretary Ruben Torres said. (TODAY)
- Moro rebel leader Nur Misuari, speaking in Cotabato City on Wednesday, promised to curb crime and corruption in the region to be created for Moslem self-rule. (TODAY)
- Residents living near the slopes of Mount Kanlaon in Negros Occidental have been told to get ready to evacuate after the volcano ejected ash again on Tuesday afternoon. (TODAY)

- The U.S. launched a second wave of cruise missiles against Iraqi military targets in southern Iraq on Wednesday, pursuing its most serious military confrontation with President Saddam Hussein since the Gulf War. (TODAY)

- Moro National Liberation Front chairman Nur Misuari's election as governor of the autonomous region in Moslem Mindanao is a foregone conclusion as his two rivals have withdrawn their candidacy. (THE PHILIPPINE JOURNAL)

- Malaysia will offer economic training to Moslems in Mindanao after the signing of a peace pact between the Moro National Liberation Front and the government, Malaysia's Bernama news agency reported. (THE PHILIPPINE JOURNAL)

- Interior and local government secretary Robert Barbers said he will leave the cabinet when President Ramos' term ends in 1998 but he is now laying the foundation that would enable the department to serve the people better beyond the year 2000. (THE PHILIPPINE JOURNAL)

- Police in San Fernando have placed the 1.4 billion peso megadike under tight security following a sabotage attempt on the project's 3.2 kilometer transverse dam, a police official said. (THE PHILIPPINE STAR)

- Heeding the repeated calls of President Ramos for the House to approve his proposed tax reforms, 120 Congressmen from the administration-backed Lakas-NUCD party decided in a caucus to pass the beer and cigarette tax bill next week. (THE PHILIPPINE STAR)

- At least 65 children in Metro Manila were admitted to hospital for diarrhea, the Department of Health said. The department said 55 of the children, 12 years and below, were taken to hospital last Sunday for severe dehydration. (MANILA BULLETIN)

- Energy officials on Thursday gave an assurance that the country has enough oil supply and that the situation did not have any immediate and direct effect on the oil industry. "I think this (U.S.-Iraq) conflict could be settled before the exhaustion of the three oil firms' stock," energy secretary Francisco Viray said. (MANILA STANDARD)
- The Bases Conversion Development Authority is looking into the possibility of re-bidding the multi-billion peso Club John Hay project. (THE BUSINESS DAILY)
- The central bank said on Wednesday that the tension in the middle east would not affect the stability of the peso. (THE BUSINESS DAILY)
